_: Task 011's record of Tempo. Same role as arc.json: this file is the source of truth, and every other file that restates a Tempo constant is checked against it by zk-verdict/scripts/tempo-constants.sh. That script checks INTERNAL AGREEMENT ONLY. It cannot tell you this record is right — which is why every entry carries how it was obtained.

wrongEndpoint.whatItActuallyIs: TEMPO MAINNET. Confirmed 2026-09-08 against https://tempo.xyz/developers/docs/quickstart/connection-details, which names 4217 as Tempo Mainnet with explorer https://explore.tempo.xyz and says to use it for 'production assets such as pathUSD, and live payment flows'.
wrongEndpoint.why: This URL appeared in search results as the Tempo RPC. The earlier wording here called it 'a DIFFERENT CHAIN', which was true and badly understated: deploying to it would have been a MAINNET deployment with real assets, which AGENTS.md §8 forbids outright. tempo-constants.sh fails if this hostname appears anywhere in the tree as an endpoint, and tempo-testnet.sh refuses to run against chain 4217 by name. Those are not tidiness checks; they are the mainnet guard.

ethGetBalance.meaning: a constant, not a balance. Tempo has no native gas token. Any test, script or page that shows funding by reading the native balance is showing a constant — use IERC20Min.balanceOf.

blockAtReadTime.note: gasLimit is ~1500x the 320,600 gas a Solana-proof settlement used on Arc. Groth16 verification is not gas-constrained here.

transactionTypes._: 213 transactions over 60 blocks ending at 0x20be4a1, read 2026-09-08.
transactionTypes.meaning: Standard legacy and EIP-1559 transactions are in active use, so upstream Foundry can send one. 0x76 is Tempo's native type and is the ONLY one that can carry an explicit feeToken; its other fields are account abstraction and multicall (calls, nonceKey, feePayerSignature, validAfter, validBefore, keyAuthorization, aaAuthorizationList). Choosing a non-default fee token needs 0x76 and therefore tempo-foundry; paying a fee does not.

receiptsNameTheFeeToken._: Every receipt carries feeToken and feePayer -- INCLUDING for a plain type 0x2 transaction.
receiptsNameTheFeeToken.meaning: 011's T-4 is satisfiable with a standard transaction. The evidence is in the receipt.

defaultFeeToken.name: PathUSD
defaultFeeToken.how: eth_call of name() / symbol() / decimals() / totalSupply(), 2026-09-08
defaultFeeToken.note: This is the token both sampled receipts paid their fee in. It answers 011's open questions 'which TIP-20' and 'what decimals' without a faucet. Six decimals -- the same as USDC on Arc -- and RecknTempoTip20.t.sol already exercises 6 and 18.

feeArithmetic._: How a fee in gas becomes a fee in the TIP-20. DERIVED from two real receipts on 2026-09-08, not from documentation.

checkedAgainst.0x6f6b5d06a1477704c5e538a200ca6b3b3f4958: gasUsed 22820 * 500600000000 / 1e12 = 11423; the receipt's own Transfer log to 0xfeec…0000 moved 11424

evmProbe._: eth_call with to:null, so TEMPO'S OWN EVM ran the path. No key, no transaction, no fee, no state written. This is NOT a deployment and it does NOT satisfy 011 T-4. Full output in tempo-evm-probe.json.
evmProbe.bytecodeIdentical: the SP1Verifier, RecknVerdictVerifier and RecknZkEscrow codehashes were compared against the local anvil control and are equal. Without that, no other row means anything.
evmProbe.reproduced: a real Groth16 proof of a real SOLANA execution released 250.000000 (6dp) to the seller and emptied the escrow -- identical to the control.
evmProbe.failed: the same machinery refunded the buyer in full on the FAILED proof. This is the PROOF-driven refund, not refundAfterDeadline.
evmProbe.bindingMismatch: a real proof of ANOTHER execution reverted with BindingMismatch() and moved nothing; the escrow still held 250.000000.
evmProbe.costOfTheWholeDemo: about 31,000,000 gas for deploy + fund + settle, which at the 500.6 gwei effectiveGasPrice seen on 2026-09-08 is about 15.5 PathUSD. tempo-testnet.sh budgets 40M.

gasSchedule._: Why the numbers above differ by 2.6x to 10.6x, measured one primitive at a time against the same control. Full output in tempo-gas-schedule.json.
gasSchedule.computeIsIdentical: bn256Pairing over two real pairs: 114,291 gas on Tempo and 114,291 on the control. bn256Add, bn256ScalarMul, keccak, SLOAD, warm SSTORE and EXTCODESIZE are all 1.00x.

stateIsNot.coldSSTORE: 254,347 on Tempo vs 22,147 on the control (11.48x)

gasSchedule.consequence: Tempo prices state growth, not computation. For an escrow whose expensive operation is a Groth16 verification that is the favourable direction: settleWithProof is only 2.6x, because it is mostly pairing. fund() is 10.6x, because it writes a Deal struct.

tip20Semantics._: The REAL PathUSD, by eth_call, against the assumptions RecknZkEscrow makes about a token. MockTIP20 was built from documentation, so until this these were assumptions. Full output in tempo-tip20-probe.json; re-run with tempo-tip20-probe.sh.
tip20Semantics.revertsNeverReturnsFalse: an underfunded transfer reverts with InsufficientBalance and a transferFrom without allowance reverts with InsufficientAllowance. This is load-bearing: RecknZkEscrow ignores the ERC-20 boolean (forge lints it), so on a false-returning token fund() would record a funded deal holding nothing.
tip20Semantics.escrowIsAValidRecipient: a transfer to an address carrying RecknZkEscrow's real runtime bytecode succeeds. InvalidRecipient does not catch ordinary contracts, so the escrow can be funded.
tip20Semantics.refusesItself: a transfer to 0x20C0…0000 reverts with InvalidRecipient -- the documented rule, measured. This is the behaviour RecknTempoTip20.t.sol's T-11 models.

faucet._: How PathUSD is obtained. No browser, no wallet connection, and NO KEY -- the address being funded does not have to be the caller's.
faucet.amountPerCall: 1,000,000.000000 of each (6 decimals). Confirmed on chain: every mint-shaped Transfer log sampled carries value 0xe8d4a51000 = 1000000000000 raw units.
faucet.existenceProbedNotAssumed: calling it with bad params returns -32602 'Invalid params'; an invented method returns -32601 'method not allowed'. The method is present on the Moderato endpoint.
faucet.source: https://tempo.xyz/developers/docs/quickstart/faucet, read 2026-09-08, plus the on-chain log count.
faucet.consequence: 011 §9.1's budget of ~50 PathUSD is met about 20,000x over by ONE call. The faucet is not the constraint. The only remaining founder action is holding a key.

verifiedEndToEnd._: The method was not only probed for existence -- it was called, and the receipts read back. This is the first transaction this project has caused on Tempo. It is a FAUCET call, not a deployment: it deploys nothing, settles nothing, and does not touch deployedByReckn.
verifiedEndToEnd.addressProvenance: a fresh Foundry keystore created by the founder; nonce was 0, no code, zero balance before the call. The agent does not hold this key and never sees it -- tempo-testnet.sh takes the keystore's NAME, never a private key.
verifiedEndToEnd.result: status 0x1 in block 0x20c1988; 1,000,000.000000 pathUSD minted, and one sibling transaction each for alphaUSD, betaUSD and thetaUSD. Only the pathUSD hash is recorded here because it is the only one anything downstream depends on -- recording four hashes to look thorough would put three values in the record that nothing checks.

foundryGasEstimation._: Measured the hard way, by a transaction that failed. Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because anyone deploying a contract to Tempo with Foundry will hit it.
foundryGasEstimation.finding: `forge script` sizes each broadcast transaction from ITS OWN LOCAL SIMULATION times --gas-estimate-multiplier (default 130), NOT from the chain's eth_estimateGas. On a chain with Ethereum's gas schedule that is fine. Here it is not: Tempo's code deposit is ~2,577 gas/byte against Ethereum's ~202 (see measured.gasSchedule), so a contract creation simulates 5-6x cheaper locally than it costs, is handed a limit that short, and burns all of it.
foundryGasEstimation.theNodeIsRight: eth_estimateGas on Tempo returned 12,783,924 for the SP1Verifier creation, against 12,986,736 measured in Tempo's own EVM. The chain knows. Foundry does not ask it.
foundryGasEstimation.failedTxDetail: SP1Verifier creation, 2026-09-08. Limit 3,425,376; gasUsed 3,425,376; status 0x0. Cost 1.714744 PathUSD for nothing. No contract exists at the address it would have taken.
foundryGasEstimation.fix: tempo-testnet.sh passes -g 1000 (10x) and refuses to start if the chain's own estimate for any creation is within 15% of the limit forge would offer. The measured ratios are 5.24x / 6.32x / 5.52x, so 10x is 1.6-1.9x of headroom. Over-sizing a gas LIMIT is free -- a transaction pays for gas used, not gas offered -- so headroom costs nothing and a short limit costs a whole deployment.
foundryGasEstimation.notAffected: `cast send` estimates against the node and is correct, so fund/settle were never at risk. Only the forge script deploy needed this.

fromDocs._: Read 2026-09-08 from https://tempo.xyz/developers/docs/protocol/tip20/spec. NOT measured. Nothing in the code depends on any of these without a test that models it.

unknown._: Still not established. Not assumed anywhere in the code. Entries that were closed are rewritten in place rather than deleted, so what was and was not known when the tests were written stays legible. The faucet moved out on 2026-09-08 -- see measured.faucet.
unknown.testnetTokenPolicy: PARTIALLY CLOSED. PathUSD answers paused() and returned false on 2026-09-08, and no TIP-403 policy refused any transfer probed. That is a reading of one moment: a token that is unpaused now can be paused later, which is the risk 011 §8 discloses rather than mitigates. The escrow is still tested against both behaviours (T-7, T-8) rather than against this reading.
unknown.realProofOnChain: PARTIALLY CLOSED. A real SP1 Groth16 proof of a Solana execution DOES verify on Tempo and does move a token -- measured in Tempo's own EVM by eth_call (see measured.evmProbe). What remains open is the half that needs a key: that a TRANSACTION carrying it can be paid for, included and persisted, and that a real TIP-20 balance moves. An eth_call writes no state and pays no fee. Nothing may be described as 'deployed on Tempo' on the strength of it.

sameCodeAsArc._: Checked by zk-verdict/scripts/tempo-arc-parity.sh, which reads eth_getCode off BOTH chains and compares byte for byte. Recorded here rather than in arc.json so that 005 owns one record and 011 owns the other.
sameCodeAsArc.whyItMeansSomething: RecknZkEscrow has no constructor and no immutable, so its deployed bytecode is a pure function of its source. Equal codehashes on two chains therefore mean the same source, not merely the same configuration. The verifier is deliberately NOT compared: it takes a vkey and an address at construction, so its code legitimately differs per deployment.
sameCodeAsArc.whatItDoesNotClaim: That the two chains adjudicate identically. They do not: the deals name different verifiers and different tokens. What is shared is the source, and the payout logic it fixes.
